scenario.name: balanced-urban-system
scenario.description: Several midsize cities prosper together, producing a more stable hierarchy than either the baseline or a primate-city regime.

scenario.name: baseline
scenario.description: Default peninsula dynamics with moderate resource rents and modest institutional drift.

scenario.name: botswana
scenario.description: Resource rents remain high, but inclusive and adaptive initial institutions soften the curse.

scenario.name: megacity-trap
scenario.description: One dominant metropolis absorbs activity early, then system-wide overstretch and weak secondary cities drag on long-run performance.

scenario.name: merchant-republic
scenario.description: Port-led city clusters coordinate through trade and capital accumulation rather than extractive rents.

scenario.name: open-cluster
scenario.description: Trade-oriented sites begin more open and get stronger spatial spillovers from nearby peers.

scenario.name: resource-curse
scenario.description: Resource-rich sites start more extractive and remain tempting long enough to become traps.

scenario.name: shock-reform
scenario.description: Early depletion shocks raise crisis pressure and create reform opportunities.

scenario.name: ucb-bait
scenario.description: Short-run resource returns spike hard while institutional decay accelerates behind them.
